title: Topsy and Mallow's Great Swap
markdown:
Deep under a giggling oak lived Topsy the bunny and Mallow the kitten. Topsy was a fluffy white puffball. His ears wiggled like question marks. His nose twitched faster than a hummingbird’s wings. He loved to dig. Dig, dig, DIG. Whoosh went the dirt. He found the greenest clover and the sunniest nap spots — though napping was not his best trick.

Mallow was sleek, fur the colour of warm milk, eyes like green marbles. He was a champion napper. Purrrrrr, like a tiny toy motor. He dreamed of butterflies and maybe a fish treat. Batting strings and pouncing on dust bunnies was important work. Digging looked messy. Why bother, when sunbeams were already warm?

One bright morning Topsy munched a super-duper clover he had just dug up. “Mmmph. Digging is easy-peasy, Mallow.”

Mallow stretched, pink tongue, little teeth, a yawn. “Easy for you. Napping takes so much skill. You have to be perfectly cozy. Purrrrrr.”

Topsy’s ears nearly touched. “Napping? Pish posh. I bet I could nap better than you. Digging is way more exciting.”

Mallow’s eyes twinkled. “You think digging is easy? It’s dusty. Yucky paws.”

That was when Topsy had a brilliantly bonkers idea. “Let’s swap. You dig for a whole day. I’ll nap for a whole day.”

Mallow’s tail flicked. “A whole day? Okay. But if I see a funny ladybug, I’m chasing it.”

“And if I find a super comfy spot,” Topsy giggled, “I might nibble clover while I’m meant to be sleeping.”

And that was that. The Great Swap of the Day began under the giggling oak.

Topsy hopped to Mallow’s favourite sunny spot by the window, warm as a golden hug. “Right. Nap time.” He tried to curl like Mallow, paws tucked, ears soft. His legs were made for running and digging, not for tucking neatly. He felt all long and wiggly. He shut his eyes. Whoosh — a little bluebird zipped past the glass. Ears shot up. Nose went twitch-twitch-twitch. “Bird,” he whispered, much too loud, forgetting every rule of napping. Then tap-tap-tap, a gentle rain. His paws practically itched to dig a tiny hole to keep his clover patch dry. Napping was so boring. He tried to purr like Mallow. It came out a funny rumbling squeak. “This is harder than it looks,” he grumbled, and gave up on the purr. He twitched his nose and watched the leaves dance. It was not a nap. Not at all.

Meanwhile, in the garden, Mallow looked at a patch of soft loamy earth and tried to sound brave. “Digging time.” He dipped a dainty paw. “Ooh, dusty,” he meowed, wrinkling his nose. Scratch, scratch. His little kitten claws only tickled the dirt. “This isn’t very exciting.” His tail drooped. Then his paw touched something wiggly. A long pink worm popped its head out. Mallow forgot digging and pounced. Boink. He batted the surprised worm until it hid again. “Wow.” He dug a little more and found a sparkly smooth pebble. He batted that too. Not deep digging. Interesting, though. A few dusty smudges on milk-coloured fur. “This is trickier than chasing a sunbeam,” he huffed.

Topsy was supposed to guard the sill with sleepy eyes. He imagined sneaky squirrels stealing cushions. He popped awake like a fluffy statue on alert. His pretend purr sounded like a rusty hinge.

Mallow’s hole stayed shallow and messy, as if he had been playing with lunch. He chased a ladybug (of course), found a blue feather that tickled, and a shiny button. No deep whoosh. He sat with a sigh and looked at his dusty paws.

Late afternoon. Sunbeams had moved on. The garden looked un-dug. Topsy’s ears drooped. Tired, but not from rest. Mallow’s whiskers drooped. Paws ached from awkward scratching.

“Awful,” Topsy said, hopping toward his old digging spot. “I can’t nap. Too quiet. My paws ache to dig.”

Mallow padded over. “I can’t dig. Scratch, scratch. I miss butterflies and snuggly sunbeams. Achoo.”

They looked at each other, glum. The burrow felt less cozy. The garden felt less magic. Two simple jobs, both failed.

Then Topsy remembered how peaceful Mallow looked asleep. “Napping is hard. It takes stillness. I can’t be still.”

Mallow looked at that twitching nose. “Digging takes knowing where to push. My paws don’t know.”

A spark. “Maybe we’re really, really good at our own jobs.”

“Maybe we can help each other.”

Topsy bounced. “You show me cozy. I’ll show you whoosh.”

And that is exactly what they did. Mallow, with all the gentle patience of a master napper, showed Topsy how to tuck his paws just so, how to find the warmest patch of golden light, and how to let out a rumbling contented purr. Topsy showed Mallow how to wiggle his nose right before closing his eyes, and how to let his ears go all soft and relaxed. Then, with Mallow snoozing soundly nearby, Topsy hopped back to the garden with new energy. He showed how to use strong back legs to push and propel, how to angle paws to scoop, and how to make a really satisfying thump as he dug deep. Mallow, watching that happy focused whoosh, finally understood. It was not only dusty boring work. It was exciting joyful work.

Soon Topsy was digging a magnificent new burrow door, the best yet. Mallow curled in the most delightful sunbeam, purring louder than a toy boat. Dig, dig, DIG — and purrrrrr — each in the right place, side by side under the giggling oak, while the ladybug went about her own important day.
